partialCapture.note:
Neither the 456-frame sweep nor the 12-theme sweep was regenerated. Frames added or refreshed here were captured against the same guards (assertFramePaints) but only in the two brand themes, and the live-app frames came from the real Electron window rather than Storybook. The spacing round REFRESHED the five chat-tool-rows surfaces because the row pitch changed under them, and added two: `spacing-uniformity` reproduces the three runs the operator screenshotted, `turn-boundary` shows the hierarchy that survives the tightening. `narrow` and `working-labels` are now captured in a viewport sized to their content — at 1280x900 they were mostly empty ground and crossed the uniformity ceiling once the rows tightened. REMEDIATION ROUND 1: all seven chat-tool-rows surfaces were refreshed again, because the name/summary gutter, the running row's live clock, the sr-only outcome text and the summary fallback all changed what they show. REMEDIATION ROUND 2: `real-conversation-tool-rows` was RE-CAPTURED and is no longer stale. It now shows 38 real tool rows with 0 blank object columns on a 20px pitch, rendered by the shipped reducer and the shipped CanonicalTranscript over real /history pages paged oldest-first in 20-entry pages (the cross-page condition the blank-summary defect needed). Electron is not required for this surface — the desktop API answers a plain bearer request. The reading was proven falsifiable by running the SAME harness with the reducer starved: stripping tool_calls alone still yields 0 blanks (the output fallback carries it), stripping tool_calls AND output yields 53 of 53 blank, reproducing the original defect from the current head.

DESIGN PROPOSAL ROUND: this round added a new surface, `chat-run-details` - eight story states of the run-details popover (docs/run-details.md), rendered as the REAL `ChatHeader` inside a chat-column ground with the panel open over a fixture roster and plan. Sixteen frames added (eight states x the two brand themes) and no existing frame touched, so `frames` and `surfaces` were raised by 16 and 8 rather than a sweep being run: a sweep would have rewritten 474 frames nobody reviewed to add eight that were. The frames were captured at viewports sized to each story, because a 384px popover on a 1280x900 page is more than 99% one colour and the uniformity ceiling rejects it - which is that guard working as designed. The two `settled`/`header-trigger` frames differ only in their fixture, so the presence and absence of the header button reads as one comparison. REMEDIATION: two corrections came out of reading the frames rather than out of a test. Radix's ScrollArea content wrapper is `display: table; min-width: 100%`, which sizes to max-content and silently defeats every `truncate` inside the panel - the first capture showed a long label pushing the whole numbers run past the panel's right edge. `todos-only` and `crowded` were then re-captured at 820px tall, because the panel's own `min(60vh, 480px)` ceiling is what those two frames are judged at and at a shorter viewport the item cap's `+4 more` row falls past the fold. One frame was also re-captured with `type="always"` on the ScrollArea to prove the viewport overflows and scrolls rather than being clipped by the Root (the thumb spanned 305px of the 475px viewport, so about 740px of content); the committed set is from the default `type="hover"`, which is why no still shows a scrollbar.

supplementary.why: The claims are a real pointer hover and a click that stages a draft. Storybook can force the revealed class but not produce the hover, and a staged draft is store state a fixture would have to fake, so these are captured from the running app against an isolated seeded backend instead. The sidebar has no story, so re-running the sweep cannot re-derive them; docs/evidence/sidebar-new-chat/README.md carries the re-capture procedure.
